children: Bitcoin dropped below $56,000 on Saturday, and Ethereum and XRP fell with it. BTC is trading at $55,693, down 8.9% in a day and 16.2% in a week. Ethereum fell 10.1% to $1,543.23 and is down 17.9% for the week. XRP lost 8.2% to $0.8701 and is down 12.4% over seven days.
Liquidations Hit as Stocks Slide

When Bitcoin broke below $57,000, its lowest level since September 2024, about $400 million in long bets were wiped out in just 10 minutes. Close to $160 billion left the crypto market in 12 hours. US stocks had a rough week too. The Nasdaq 100 had its biggest weekly fall since the Covid crash in March 2020.
Other big coins fell just as hard:
BNB dropped 10% to $510.86 and is down 17.3% for the week.
Solana fell 9.1% to $65.32 and is down 13% for the week.
Tether and USD Coin stayed near $1.
Has the Bear Market Already Started?

Counted from Bitcoin’s record high of about $126,198 in October 2025, the bear market is already about 409 days old. The 2013 to 2015 bear market ended after about 410 days, so a new low this week would make this one the longest in Bitcoin’s history.

This drop has been shallower than earlier ones, though. Bitcoin is down about 55% from its peak. Past bear markets took it down 76% to 85%. A 76% fall from the 2025 high would mean a price near $30,000. A fall as big as the 2013 to 2015 one would take it close to $20,000.
ETF Money Keeps Leaving

Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost about $300 million in one day and nearly $600 million the next. Apart from one flat day, money has flowed out of these funds for 10 trading days in a row. Bitcoin miners are also said to be selling.
What the Charts Show

Bitcoin’s fall below $61,500 took it straight into the support zone of $58,000 to $56,000. It is now below that zone, and the next support area sits between $53,000 and $50,000. Large groups of leveraged positions sit near $56,000, $51,000 and $50,700, and those levels could pull the price lower.

On short-term charts, Bitcoin keeps making lower lows. Bears now need to defend $64,000. A move above that would be the first sign the trend is turning. One early sign of a possible bounce is showing on the RSI, but it needs two green daily candles in a row to confirm. If the price closes below its latest low, that signal is cancelled. Until there is a clear turn, such as a trendline break or a big daily wick on heavy volume, the trend stays down.
Is the Four-Year Cycle Breaking?

There is a growing worry that this is not a normal dip in Bitcoin’s four-year cycle. In the worst case, Bitcoin could be going through a much bigger correction of its whole price history since 2010. That would need three things to keep happening:
the US dollar staying strong
US stocks falling further
big holders on Binance continuing to sell
There are a few reasons this time looks different:
Since spot ETFs launched in January 2024, more Bitcoin is held by large institutions, and its price now moves more with the wider economy.
Several on-chain tools that called past tops missed last year’s peak.
If 2026 ends in the red, Bitcoin will have lost money two years in a row for the first time.
The dollar usually weakened when crypto fear was high. This time it is getting stronger on talk of US rate hikes.
Bitcoin’s long-term chart is starting to look like an ending diagonal pattern.

Market opinion on the cycle has also flipped. Earlier this year, many said the four-year cycle was over and prices would rise faster. Now that prices are falling, many say the cycle still holds, because that would mean a bottom is close.

title: Crypto Market Bloodbath: Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP Crash Up to 10% as Bear Market Fears Grow
